text: 27-year-old male. The patient reports a sustained sensation of the room spinning since this morning, which is low grade and constant. He occasionally feels nauseous and has taken diphenhydramine to help him sleep, which also alleviates his symptoms slightly. He mentions recent increased intake of garlic due to trying to recover from a cold a few days ago. Past medical history is unremarkable.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sustained sensation of the room spinning. I also have Occasional nausea, Use of diphenhydramine for symptoms and to aid sleep, Recent cold. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Multiple sclerosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for clarifying; please ignore the previous suggestion of Multiple Sclerosis, as your symptoms of a spinning room and recent cold strongly suggest a vestibular issue. Has this spinning sensation worsened in the last few hours or days, or is it constant?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Generally healthy with no significant past medical history. Social history: Does not specify any social habits including smoking, alcohol use, or recreational drug use.
